agree.reason: The salon specialism and plain admissions will appeal to her, but the page never gives her a reason to pay about $2,388 a year when her cousin charges $600, or to see that she can keep him, so a reader who resists has little reason to book.

honest.reason: Nearly every claim follows the brief, but "One saved $800" drops the fact that the client only said she did.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the raw numbers without working them: no annual cost, no 29 of 31 retained, and no 9 of 31 share. It also leaves out that the price went up because payroll was added, so the increase looks arbitrary.

right_comparison.reason: Her real alternative is a once-a-year tax-time bookkeeper at $600, and the page answers it only with a generic accountant fixing messy books, never saying that her own accountant or cousin keeps doing her returns.

qualification.reason: It admits three missed deadlines but leaves out the remedy (that month's fee is free since January), so the hedge has no consequence the reader can hold Carla to, and the hedge on accountant savings is vague.

objections.reason: The main objections (cost compared with her cousin, loyalty to him, being locked in) go unanswered, even though the no-contract 30-day notice and the fact that the cousin can keep doing her taxes were there to use.

fit.reason: It runs about 330 words of sales-page text with clear sections and ends on the booking button, as the brief asked.
